Ketubot 2a_5-6.note: Exactly. This is a legal discussion about hypothetical cases.

Ketubot 2b_11-11.note: This is a story, as it has events and change. It is correct that the rabbi, Shmuel, is not a character in the story. The story is about an anonymous man, "a certain man." Stories can be about unnamed people. The story ends with the man's statement. Shmuel's ruling is a legal ruling that need not be quoted with the story.

Ketubot 3a_9-10.note: This is the same story as on Ketubot 2b, the previous selection. It happen to be quoted on both pages. The boundaries of the story should be the same too. It should end with the man's statement. And iוּנְסָא דִּשְׁכִיחַ — שָׁאנֵי, דְּכֵיוָן דְּאִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְאַתְנוֹיֵי וְלָא אַתְנִי, אִיהוּ הוּא דְּאַפְסֵיד אַנַּפְשֵׁיהּ. This is the Talmud's rejection of the proof from the story and not part of the story. t should certain not have the last line,

Ketubot 4a_0-1.note: This is a legal ruling, not a description of any real event. It is what a groom should do under these circumstances

Ketubot 4a_2-4.note: This is a legal discussion and a legal ruling. Not a story about real events

Ketubot 5a_10-12.note: There are not really multiple events here. It is just multiple statement. The Rabbis are stating traditions. And there are verbal objections, but it is all talk

Ketubot 7b_5-5.note: correct. It is a report of what one rabbi said to another rabbi, ordering him to go and do something. But there are no events

Ketubot 8a_9-9.note: Yes, the change is minimal. It is a borderline story. But the erasoning is correct.

Ketubot 8b_3-5.note: This is indeed a story but the selection is only half the story. It is cut off in mid dialogue. The rest of the story is in the next selection, but these should be combined into one story.

Ketubot 8b_6-10.note: This is the second half of the story that with Ketubot 8b (segments 3-5). It is one long story

Ketubot 8b_11-12.note: It is a legal ruling stating what the sages "instituted," that is, they ruled this should be done.

Ketubot 8b_13-13.note: correct, but the story ends with  לְהוֹצִיא בִּכְלֵי פִשְׁתָּן. Rav Pappa's statement is not part of the story. It is a comment on the story.

Ketubot 9b_0-0.note: Yes. It is also during biblical times. "David" here is King David

Ketubot 10a_7-8.note: The fact that the man is unnamed is fine. It is just an unnamed man as character. THe story should end with Rav Nahman's command to flog the man. The next line (beginning with וְהָא) is the Talmud's question and not part of the story.

Ketubot 10a_9-10.note: Again, it is perfectly find to have an anonymous character. This is a borderline story since it is mainly speech acts, not really events.

Ketubot 10a_11-11.note: This is definitely a story. Multiple events and causality

Ketubot 10b_1-1.note: This is definitely a story. There are multiple events in a causal relationship. The end of the story implies change: that the man can maintain his marriage and need not suspect or divorce the woman.

Ketubot 10b_3-3.note: This is definitely a story. The anonymous character does not weaken the confidence. Ther eis a temporal progression: after the woman and man come to Rabban Gamliel he checks about her family.

Ketubot 10b_6-6.note: This too is a story. There is causality and temporal progression: after the woman speak to the rabbi he takes them to a bathhouse and feeds them, and then checks the woman again. The outcome is a change too

Ketubot 12a_8-9.note: Correct. This is a description of a customary practice. Not a story about specific people or characters.

Ketubot 12b_0-0.note: Correct. This is a borderline It lacks specificity.  It also starts in the previous line (0n 12a) with Rav Ashi's statement. This is the second half of his statement. But it has change and temporal progresion. So "low confidence" is perfect

Ketubot 12b_4-4.note: It is also a legal ruling, a hypothetical legal case. Not a story

Ketubot 40b_11-11.note: The events here are rabbis making legal arguments. True, one rabbi went to the place of another rabbi to recite his tradition. But that is not really an event that makes for a story.

Ketubot 42b_8-8.note: The main actions, experiencing difficulty and "resolving" a difficult legal issue, are not events, but just parts of a legal dicussion.

Ketubot 49b_6-6.note: This is a borderline story. It is basically one event, though two verbs are used. He forced a man to give charity. Also , the first part of the excerpt (וְלָא אֲמַרַן, אֶלָּא דְּלָא אֲמִיד, אֲבָל אֲמִיד — כָּפֵינַן לֵיהּ עַל כֻּרְחֵיהּ.) is not part of the story.

Ketubot 49b_9-10.note: Ravin sending a letter is just one event.  R. Yehudah son of the sister of R. Yosi is responding to a different case and just tells of the legal ruling. He does not tell a story, but tell what the sage ruled.

Ketubot 49b_4-4.note: Correct, Rav Hisda is making a legal ruling about what you should say to such a man.

Ketubot 50a_0-0.note: But the following section  וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לְבַזְבֵּז [יוֹתֵר מֵחוֹמֶשׁ], וְלֹא הִנִּיחַ לוֹ חֲבֵירוֹ. וּמַנּוּ — רַבִּי יְשֵׁבָב. וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: רַבִּי יְשֵׁבָב, וְלֹא הִנִּיחוֹ חֲבֵירוֹ, וּמַנּוּ — רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא. could be considered a borderline story

Ketubot 50b_4-5.note: correct. It is a legal discussion with legal reasoning.

Ketubot 50b_6-6.note: This is a borderline story. The reasoning is correct that there is minimal causality. But there is some, and some change. It should be marked a borderline story.

Ketubot 50b_9-10.note: This should be marked a borderline story, since it is just one real event and then discussion

Ketubot 51a_1-2.note: This should be marked a borderline story, since there is really just one event, then a legal discussion.

Ketubot 51b_7-9.note: This is just a theoretical discussion. Shmuel is not talking about an event that happened, but a legal case.

Ketubot 52a_13-14.note: There are no real events. Levi thought about acting according to a certain opinion. But Rav told him otherwise. No events

Ketubot 52b_4-5.note: Excellent. The story should start with the word קָרִיבֵיהּ. The sentence before it is a legal ruling. It is relevant to the story, but not part of the story. The story should be marked a borderline story since it is mainly talk

Ketubot 52b_17-17.note: This is the beginning of a story that continues on the next page of Talmud, the next selection here, Ketubot 53a (Segments 0-3)

Ketubot 53a_0-3.note: This is the second half of the story that should go with the previous segment from the previous page of Talmud, 52b

Ketubot 53a_12-13.note: Yes, this could be a borderline story. Basically one event and a discussion about it.

Ketubot 53b_0-0.note: This line is the continuation of the statement from the previous Talmud page. it should not be marked separately.

Ketubot 54a_13-14.note: This should be marked a borderline story, since there is basically one event and then a legal ruling and discussion

Ketubot 54a_20-20.note: This is a high confidence story. There is a temporal progression, in that the daughter-in-law was bringing orphans to court, and then she went and dressed

Ketubot 54a_21-21.note: This should be marked a borderline story. There is a temporal progression, in that someone order a dowry be given to his daughter and then (as a later time) the dowry depreciated. There is weak causality, as the result of the depreciated dowry is just a ruling by a rabbi.

Ketubot 54a_22-22.note: The story finished on the next page of Talmud with one more line, and it is a borderline story

Ketubot 55a_7-7.note: Not a story at all.  This is a legal debate between Pumbedita and matta Mehasia.

Ketubot 56a_2-2.note: This is a legal debate. There is a setting for the debate of one sage sitting before another. But it is just a debate

Ketubot 56b_11-11.note: This is the beginning of a story that continues on the next page of Talmud

Ketubot 57a_0-0.note: This is a borderline story but it begins with the last line of the previous page of Talmud. This is the continuation of that story

Ketubot 60a_2-2.note: This is indeed a story but the last line should not be included. That is a follow-up question. that comes after the story.  ( סוֹמֵא מְנָא יָדַע? אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: בְּרֵיחָא וּבְטַעְמָא. is not part of the story)

Ketubot 60b_2-3.note: This is a story. But too much is quoted at the beginning and not enough at the end. The line אָמַר עוּלָּא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה. וְאָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא: לִי הִתִּיר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא לָשֵׂאת לְאַחַר חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ is not part of the story. It is a legal ruling. And Abaye's statement at the end is part of the story since he refers to the story direclty (אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַאי מִילְּתָא דַאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן אֲפִילּוּ בֵּיעֲתָא בְּכוּתָּחָא לָא לִישְׁרֵי אִינִישׁ בִּמְקוֹם רַבֵּיהּ, לָא מִשּׁוּם דְּמִיחֲזֵי כְּאַפְקִירוּתָא, אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא מִסְתַּיְּיעָא מִילְּתָא לְמֵימְרָא. דְּהָא אֲנָא הֲוָה גְּמִירְנָא לֵיהּ לְהָא דְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל, אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לָא מִסְתַּיְּיעָא לִי מִילְּתָא לְמֵימַר.)

Ketubot 60b_5-6.note: This should be marked as a borderline story. There is mainly dialogue. But events are mentioned.

Ketubot 60b_7-9.note: The names characters are simply involved in legal discussion. The only story is הֲוָה עוֹבָדָא וַחֲנַקְתֵּיהּ. וְלָא הִיא, הָהִיא שׁוֹטָה הֲוַאי, דְּלָא עָבְדִי נְשֵׁי דְּחָנְקָן בְּנַיְיהוּ. This could be identified as a borderline story. But the rest should not be identified as part of the story
